title: A Planet Beyond Our Solar System

paragraphs.en: For centuries, astronomers wondered whether other stars might have planets like our own. It was only a guess, for no one had ever seen one. Then, in the autumn of 1995, a Swiss team announced an astonishing discovery: they had detected a planet orbiting the star 51 Pegasi.
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪以来，天文学家一直想知道其他恒星是否也拥有像我们这样的行星。这仅仅是个猜测，因为从来没有人见过一颗。随后，在1995年秋天，一个瑞士团队宣布了一个惊人的发现：他们探测到一颗行星正在绕飞马座51恒星运行。

vocabulary.example: I wondered what lay beyond the horizon.
vocabulary.derivatives: wonder (v.) → wonderful (adj.) 奇妙的 → wonderment (n.) 惊奇

vocabulary.example: The telescope detected a faint signal from the galaxy.
vocabulary.derivatives: detect (v.) → detection (n.) 探测 → detective (n.) 侦探

vocabulary.example: The moon is orbiting the Earth.
vocabulary.derivatives: orbit (n./v.) → orbital (adj.) 轨道的 → orbiter (n.) 轨道飞行器

difficult_sentences.en: It was only a guess, for no one had ever seen one.
difficult_sentences.zh: 这仅仅是个猜测，因为从来没有人见过一颗。
difficult_sentences.grammar: 并列句，由for连接表原因。had ever seen为过去完成时，表示到过去某一时间点之前从未见过。
difficult_sentences.pattern: It was only + 名词, for + 从句 (表示原因)
difficult_sentences.note: for在此是连词，用法较为正式，常表示补充说明原因，语气比because弱。

天文学家想知道

chunks.zh: 其他恒星是否可能拥有像我们这样的行星
这仅仅是个猜测

chunks.en: for no one had ever seen one
chunks.zh: 因为从来没有人见过一颗

points.explanation: 表示在过去某个时间点之前已经发生的动作。本句中had ever seen用于强调在1995年之前从未观测到。
points.example_sentence: It was only a guess, for no one had ever seen one.
points.common_mistake: ❌ I have seen it yesterday. → ✅ I saw it yesterday. (过去完成时需配合过去时间)
points.contrast: 现在完成时与过去完成时：现在完成时强调对现在的影响，过去完成时强调过去的过去。

paragraphs.en: This planet, named 51 Pegasi b, is nothing like Earth. It is a gas giant half the mass of Jupiter, yet it orbits its star every four days—far closer than Mercury is to the Sun. Its surface temperature reaches over 1,000°C. Such a 'hot Jupiter' surprised everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 这颗名为飞马座51b的行星与地球截然不同。它是一颗气态巨行星，质量是木星的一半，却每四天绕其恒星一周——比水星离太阳还要近得多。其表面温度高达1000°C以上。这样一颗“热木星”令所有人震惊。

vocabulary.example: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants.
vocabulary.derivatives: gas (n.) 气体 + giant (n.) 巨人 → gas giant (复合名词)

vocabulary.example: The mass of the object determines its gravitational pull.
vocabulary.derivatives: mass (n.) → massive (adj.) 巨大的 → massless (adj.) 无质量的

vocabulary.example: The surface temperature of Venus is extremely high.
vocabulary.derivatives: surface (n.) 表面 + temperature (n.) 温度 → surface temperature (复合名词)

difficult_sentences.en: It is a gas giant half the mass of Jupiter, yet it orbits its star every four days—far closer than Mercury is to the Sun.
difficult_sentences.zh: 它是一颗气态巨行星，质量是木星的一半，却每四天绕其恒星一周——比水星离太阳还要近得多。
difficult_sentences.grammar: 主句为It is...，后接名词短语half the mass of Jupiter作同位语。yet连接转折并列分句，破折号后为补充说明，far closer than...为比较级结构。
difficult_sentences.pattern: It is + 名词 + (同位语), yet + 主谓结构 — 比较级 + than + 从句
difficult_sentences.note: far修饰比较级表程度，意为“...得多”。

chunks.zh: 这颗名为飞马座51b的行星
chunks.function: 主语+定语（过去分词短语）

chunks.zh: 与地球截然不同

chunks.en: It is a gas giant half the mass of Jupiter
chunks.zh: 它是一颗质量是木星一半的气态巨行星

chunks.en: yet it orbits its star every four days
chunks.zh: 却每四天绕其恒星一周

chunks.en: far closer than Mercury is to the Sun
chunks.zh: 比水星离太阳还要近得多

points.explanation: 用于比较两个事物。本句中far closer than Mercury is to the Sun，省略了主谓(is close to the Sun)。
points.example_sentence: far closer than Mercury is to the Sun
points.common_mistake: ❌ It is more close than... → ✅ It is closer than... (close的比较级是closer)
points.contrast: as...as…表示同级比较，than表示超越比较。

paragraphs.en: The discovery of 51 Pegasi b revolutionized astronomy. It proved that planets could form in very different ways from our Solar System. Since then, thousands of exoplanets have been found, many of them bizarre worlds—some with two suns, others made entirely of diamond.
paragraphs.zh: 飞马座51b的发现彻底改变了天文学。它证明了行星可以以与我们太阳系截然不同的方式形成。自那以后，数千颗系外行星被发现，其中许多是奇异的世界——有些拥有两个太阳，另一些完全由钻石构成。

vocabulary.derivatives: revolution (n.) 革命 → revolutionize (v.) 彻底改变 → revolutionary (adj.) 革命性的

vocabulary.example: Exoplanets are planets that orbit stars beyond our Sun.
The creature had a bizarre appearance.
vocabulary.derivatives: bizarre (adj.) → bizarrely (adv.) 古怪地 → bizarreness (n.) 奇异

difficult_sentences.en: Since then, thousands of exoplanets have been found, many of them bizarre worlds—some with two suns, others made entirely of diamond.
difficult_sentences.zh: 自那以后，数千颗系外行星被发现，其中许多是奇异的世界——有些拥有两个太阳，另一些完全由钻石构成。
difficult_sentences.grammar: 主句为现在完成时的被动语态，后接独立主格结构many of them bizarre worlds（名词+名词短语作独立主格），破折号后为补充说明，由some...others...构成并列。
difficult_sentences.pattern: Since + 时间, 主语 + have/has been + 过去分词, 独立主格结构 — some..., others...
difficult_sentences.note: 独立主格结构常用来说明伴随状态，逻辑主语与主句主语不同。

彻底改变了天文学

chunks.en: It proved that planets could form in very different ways
chunks.zh: 它证明了行星可以以截然不同的方式形成

chunks.en: Since then, thousands of exoplanets have been found
chunks.zh: 自那以后，数千颗系外行星被发现
chunks.function: 时间状语+主句（被动语态）

chunks.zh: 其中许多是奇异的世界

points.explanation: 由名词/代词+分词/形容词/名词短语构成，在句中作状语，表示伴随状态。本句many of them bizarre worlds中，逻辑主语many of them + 名词短语bizarre worlds。
points.common_mistake: ❌ Many of them are bizarre worlds, scientists... (误作独立句) → ✅ Many of them bizarre worlds (独立主格)
points.contrast: 独立主格与分词状语：分词状语的主语通常与主句主语一致，独立主格有自己的主语。

paragraphs.en: Today, astronomers continue the search for Earth-like planets. The James Webb Space Telescope can analyse the atmospheres of distant worlds. Perhaps one day we will find a planet with signs of life. Each new discovery brings us closer to answering the age-old question: Are we alone?
paragraphs.zh: 如今，天文学家继续搜寻类地行星。詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜能分析遥远世界的大气成分。也许有一天我们会找到一颗有生命迹象的行星。每一个新发现都让我们更接近回答那个古老的问题：我们是孤独的吗？

vocabulary.example: Scientists analyse the data to draw conclusions.
vocabulary.derivatives: analyse (v.) → analysis (n.) 分析 → analytical (adj.) 分析性的

vocabulary.example: The atmospheres of Venus and Mars are mostly carbon dioxide.
vocabulary.derivatives: atmosphere (n.) → atmospheric (adj.) 大气的 → atmospherics (n.) 大气干扰

vocabulary.meaning: adj. 古老的；存在已久的
vocabulary.example: The age-old question about the origin of the universe still puzzles us.
vocabulary.derivatives: age (n.) 年龄 + old (adj.) 老的 → age-old (复合形容词)

difficult_sentences.en: Each new discovery brings us closer to answering the age-old question: Are we alone?
difficult_sentences.zh: 每一个新发现都让我们更接近回答那个古老的问题：我们是孤独的吗？
difficult_sentences.grammar: 主句主语Each new discovery，谓语brings，双宾语结构us（间接宾语）和closer to answering...（直接宾语，其中to answering为动名词短语作宾语）。冒号后为同位语从句，直接引出问题。
difficult_sentences.pattern: 主语 + bring + 人 + closer to + 动名词短语 + : + 名词从句
difficult_sentences.note: bring sb closer to doing sth意为“使某人更接近做某事”。

我们是孤独的吗？

points.explanation: bring + 宾语 + 补足语（形容词或介词短语）。本句中closer to answering...作宾补，说明宾语us的状态。
points.example_sentence: Each new discovery brings us closer to answering the age-old question.
points.common_mistake: ❌ bring us closer to answer the question → ✅ bring us closer to answering (to是介词，后跟动名词)
points.contrast: bring sth to sb（带来某物给某人）与bring sb to do sth（促使某人做某事）结构不同。
